lessons_used: Predictions continue to be consistently too high relative to measured results across almost all tests.
Evidence is still thin for adoption redesign changes, as there is only one test so far.
Evidence is still thin for choose_path copy changes as results disagree after noise correction, and thin for choose_path redesign with only one test.
Evidence is still thin for finish changes (copy, new_screen, redesign), with only one test for each.
Evidence is still thin for home changes (new_flow, redesign, wait_info), with only one test for each and no clear effect seen for home redesign.
Evidence is still thin for sign_in hint changes, with only one test so far.

candidates.title: Companion Selection Carousel View
candidates.change: Redesign pet choices into a smooth horizontal carousel layout with interactive preview animations before adoption.
candidates.why: Adoption conversion drops to 66.2% and median adoption time is 89s. Giving a clear carousel preview keeps users engaged during pet selection.

guard.reason: replacement for 'pick_friend.pet_choices' does not do the job: needs 1 of ['choice_cards'] with real words

candidates.title: Desktop Shortcut Reference Sheet
candidates.change: Add a new onboarding screen right after home intro summarizing keyboard and mouse shortcuts for controlling the pet.
candidates.why: Support received multiple emails about confusion on how to control, hide, or talk to the pet after onboarding, and finish completion is only 64.8%.

new_shortcut_guide.headline: Quick Desktop Shortcuts
new_shortcut_guide.body: Learn how to summon, move, and chat with your pet anywhere on your desktop screen.

guard.reason: Adds a new shortcut guide screen after home_intro, which is permitted inside onboarding.

candidates.score_note: Finish step has high drop-off (35.2%) and support emails, but adding new screens at finish previously decreased conversion (-1.0%).

candidates.title: Waiting Room Tip Carousel Spotlight
candidates.change: Redesign the waiting screen into a spotlight layout featuring interactive tip carousels about desktop pet controls and active progress indicators.
candidates.why: Home median time is 201s with drop-offs occurring while pet generation renders. Providing useful tips keeps users engaged during waiting.

components.text: Did you know? You can drag your pet anywhere on screen!

guard.reason: Redesigns the waiting screen layout while keeping progress and time indicators intact.

candidates.score_note: Home drop-off is relatively low (18.7%), and while home redesign showed +2.3% in 1 test, redesign cost is high.

candidates.title: Custom Photo Live Validation Flow
candidates.change: Introduce a new verification screen before generating a custom pet that displays a live animated preview of how the photo maps to the pet model.
candidates.why: Support reported 3 emails regarding custom pet generation failing or looking wrong, causing drop-offs during adoption.

new_photo_preview.headline: Preview Your Custom Pet
new_photo_preview.body: Check how your uploaded pet image will render on your desktop background.

guard.reason: Adds a custom photo preview step inside the onboarding flow.

candidates.score_note: Adoption has high drop-off (33.8%) and support reports issues, with past adoption redesign showing positive lift (+4.2%).

candidates.title: Account Save Protection Copy
candidates.change: Update sign-in headline and body copy to explicitly inform users that signing in saves pet progress across sessions and avoids pet resets.
candidates.why: 8 support emails reported pets missing or reset after signing in again, making account save protection critical at sign-in step.

sign_in.headline: Sign In to Save Your Pet Progress
sign_in.body: Keep your pet safe and accessible across sessions. Protect your companion from accidental resets.

guard.reason: Updates sign-in copy to clarify session progress saving without violating rules.

candidates.score_note: Strong support email evidence (8 emails) and low cost (copy only), though copy predictions should remain conservative.

candidates.title: Desktop Pet Rendering Progress Indicator
candidates.change: Add detailed stage status text and desktop ready notification options on the waiting screen while the pet model renders on screen.
candidates.why: Support received 3 emails about pets not appearing on desktop after waiting, and waiting time has high median duration (201s).

waiting.headline: Preparing Pet for Desktop Launch...
waiting.body: Your companion is rendering and getting ready to jump onto your desktop.

guard.reason: Adds detailed rendering status and progress indicators to the waiting screen.

candidates.score_note: Addresses high median waiting duration (201s) and support feedback, but past home wait_info test yielded negligible lift (+0.1%).

candidates.title: Desktop Completion Companion Gift
candidates.change: Display a completion reward badge and mascot on the home_intro screen giving users a free companion item upon completing onboarding.
candidates.why: Finish step conversion is 64.8% and overall onboarding finish is only 19.4%; an instant reward encourages final stage completion.

home_intro.headline: Welcome Home! Free Companion Item Unlocked
home_intro.body: Your pet is now active on your desktop with a special launch reward!

guard.reason: Mentions a 'Free Companion Item' and starter gift in onboarding copy, violating Rule 3.

candidates.title: Path Selector Adoption Speed Hint
candidates.change: Add a hint beneath path selection options highlighting that preset companions launch instantly while custom pets take under 2 minutes.
candidates.why: choose_path drop-off leaves 23.8% behind with high mean duration (514s); clear timing expectations prevent hesitation.

choose_path.hint: Preset companions launch instantly! Custom photo pets take under 2 minutes.

guard.reason: Adds an informational hint about companion launch speeds to the path selection screen.

candidates.score_note: Targets high mean duration (514s) at choose_path with low implementation cost, but choose_path copy tests showed slight negative lift (-0.3%).

candidates.title: Desktop Active Layer Visibility Banner
candidates.change: Add a prompt and status badge on home_intro confirming that the pet is running on top of open desktop windows.
candidates.why: Support received 3 emails about pets not showing on desktop or app not opening after completing setup.

home_intro.hint: Pet active! Check your taskbar or main monitor if hidden behind full-screen windows.

guard.reason: Adds active status prompt and badge to the home_intro screen.

candidates.score_note: Targets high drop-off finish step (35.2%) supported by 3 support emails, with moderate UI cost.

candidates.title: Story Screen Hero Full Bleed Layout
candidates.change: Change the initial story screen layout to full bleed with an engaging mascot asset and prominent adoption journey call to action.
candidates.why: choose_path step takes long mean duration (514s) and story engagement can be improved with a high-impact intro visual.

story.headline: Bring Your Desktop to Life
story.body: Adopt a virtual companion that lives on your desktop, reacts to your day, and keeps you company.

guard.reason: Redesigns the story screen to full bleed while preserving its intro function.

candidates.score_note: Lacks support email evidence and choose_path redesigns previously reduced conversion (-2.8%).

lessons_next: Predictions remain consistently too high relative to measured results across most tests.
For home redesign changes, 2 tests agree on slight positive noise-corrected lift, but no clear effect was seen as neither test reached significance.
Evidence is still thin for choose_path copy changes because the 2 test results disagree after noise correction (+2.8% vs -3.5%).
Evidence is still thin for adoption changes (redesign, new_flow) with only 1 test each, though adoption redesign produced the only confirmed win.
Evidence is still thin for finish changes (copy, new_screen, notification, redesign) due to having only 1 test for each type.
Evidence is still thin for sign_in changes (copy, hint) and choose_path hint/redesign changes, as each has only 1 test so far.
